 Jarrett Allen (knee) is available for Thursday’s game against the 76ers. 
 Listed as questionable on the Cavaliers’ initial injury report for Thursday, Allen is good to go. He’ll start alongside James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson and Evan Mobley.

 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Jarrett Allen lit up the Nets with 21 points (7-of-8 FGs), eight rebounds, two steals, one block and one three-pointer on Saturday. 
 Allen only hit one three-pointer last season, and the last time he hit more than one in a single year was during the 2020-21 season. He got his triple out of the way early this year. Perhaps he’ll get more than that throughout the year, but managers shouldn’t expect it. However, the efficient field goal percentage, rebounds and defensive production are all things he can provide consistently, though this was certainly a high-level outing for him. 
 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jarrett Allen (knee) recorded 14 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two blocks in Thursday’s loss to the 76ers. 
 Allen entered Thursday’s season opener with right knee patellar tendinitis, but the veteran center took on his usual role in Philadelphia. He did most of his damage before halftime, scoring 14 points and grabbing five rebounds. After halftime, Allen didn’t score and recorded just two rebounds and two blocks. Like many of his teammates who also struggled in the second half, Allen has to be more consistent. Given the fantasy track record, managers should not be concerned after Game 1. 
 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Cavs reporter Chris Fedor reports that Jarrett Allen says he will play against the 76ers on Thursday. 
 Allen has been dealing with right patellar tendinopathy, but he attended Thursday’s shootaround and said that he expects to play. In three matchups with the 76ers last season, Allen averaged 14.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.3 “stocks.” 
 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jarrett Allen (knee) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the 76ers. 
 Allen is dealing with right patellar tendinopathy, which may keep him out of the Cavaliers’ season opener. If he can’t play, Evan Mobley would slide into the center position, with Jaylon Tyson a prime candidate to move into the starting lineup. If Tyson starts, he would be worth streaming on a two-game night. 
 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jarrett Allen notched six points (3-of-5 FGs), four rebounds and two steals in Thursday’s exhibition against the Celtics. 
 With frontcourt sidekick Evan Mobley’s emergence, Allen’s fantasy ceiling has been lower in recent years. However, his floor remains relatively safe, especially with point guard James Harden in the fold for the entire season. Allen logged 17 minutes in Thursday’s preseason opener, so there isn’t much to be taken from his final stat line. 
 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jarrett Allen accounted for six points (3-of-5 FGs), three rebounds, one assist, two steals and two blocks in Monday’s Game 4 loss to the Knicks. 
 While Allen was able to put up some numbers defensively in Game 4, he offered little else in the 130-93 defeat. After going on an 18-0 run during Game 3, the Knicks blew open Monday’s series finale with a 20-0 run to send Cleveland into the offseason. The franchise can sell the fact of reaching the conference finals for the first time since 2018 as progress, and that would be accurate. However, the way Cleveland was dominated after Game 1 will raise questions. Playing in a lineup that includes Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Evan Mobley limits Allen’s fantasy ceiling. Still, he should once again offer a relatively safe top-75 floor if the Cavaliers decide to run it back with this core. 
 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jarrett Allen recorded 13 points (5-of-10 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, one steal and two blocked shots in Thursday’s Game 2 loss to the Knicks. 
 After a pedestrian 10-point, seven-rebound effort in Game 1, Allen recorded his first double-double since Game 5 of the Detroit series on Thursday. He was also reasonably productive as a defender, recording three defensive contributions. However, Cleveland’s inability to knock down shots eliminated their chances of winning, especially as the Knicks went on an 18-0 run in the third quarter. Allen and the Cavaliers will look to rebound when they host Game 3 on Saturday. 
 Jarrett Allen 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jarrett Allen tallied 23 points (8-of-14 FGs, 7-of-13 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, one steal and one blocked shot in Sunday’s Game 7 win over the Pistons. 
 As he did in Cleveland’s first-round series against Toronto, Allen saved his best for last as the Cavs earned their first Eastern Conference Finals appearance since 2018. The Cavaliers’ starting center thoroughly outplayed Jalen Duren, and his stat line lacked only a three-pointer. In the Game 7 win over Toronto in the first round, Allen put up 22 points, 19 rebounds, two steals and three blocks. Things won’t get easier for Allen and the Cavaliers, as they visit the Knicks in Game 1 of the conference finals on Tuesday. 
 Evan Mobley 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #4 
 Evan Mobley recorded 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s Game 6 loss to the Pistons. 
 Mobley recorded a complete stat line on Friday, but it wasn’t enough to compensate for Cleveland’s 19 turnovers, which Detroit converted into 25 points. Last season’s Defensive Player of the Year has put up impressive numbers this series, totaling nine steals and 17 blocks through six games. Jarrett Allen (13/8/1/1/1) also recorded solid numbers in Game 6, and the Cavaliers will need more of the same in Sunday’s decisive Game 7 in Detroit. 
 Evan Mobley 
 CLE 
 Center 
 #4 
 Evan Mobley accounted for 13 points (4-of-6 FGs, 5-of-10 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists and two blocks in Saturday’s Game 3 win over the Pistons. 
 James Harden wasn’t the only Cavaliers star heavily criticized for his play in the first two games of this series. After a decent showing in Game 1, the Cavaliers forward/center grabbed just one rebound in Game 2. While Mobley didn’t have the best afternoon scoring-wise, he was far more active defensively and on the boards. Jarrett Allen supplied the offense, tallying 18 points along with four rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocked shots. Cleveland will look to even the series at two games apiece with a win in Game 4 on Monday.

 Ja Morant accounted for 23 points (9-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Lakers.
 Sure, the Trail Blazers have played only three games, but they haven’t had any issues with how they distribute offensive responsibilities.  Duncan Robinson finished Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks with 12 points (4-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers.
 Robinson entered Tuesday averaging 19.7 points and 5.0 three-pointers per game. The Knicks focused more on him defensively, and the Pistons’ wing had a rough night. Robinson shot 0-of-8 from the field in the first half and missed all six of his three-point attempts. He got a couple to fall in the second half, but the final return wasn’t what fantasy managers hoped for.

The good news for fantasy managers was that he put up quality rebound and assist numbers, finishing one board and two helpers shy of a triple-double.
